quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Allow you to see clearly to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Fit tight enough that glasses cannot fit underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should have no scratches, resist penetration, give clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: Proper lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid wind blasts and blind spots, and avoid hazards on the road. It also stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Flash your brake light when:

options.text: You are slowing down where other drivers won't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice it. Flash it before slowing down in places they won't expect, like the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs showing road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow these regulatory signs.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may finish the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen within posted speed limits and only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually releasing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not brake, as it may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: To lower your chances of crashing, you should:

options.text: Use turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, you should be visible, tell others your plans, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look at least 12 seconds ahead, spot and avoid hazards, and be ready for changing road conditions.

questions.question: To keep control of your motorcycle while turning:

options.text: Speed up before you enter the turn.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which clothing item will not reduce crash injuries?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use strong, durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Works as well as a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not give the same protection as goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay out of the left side of the lane.
Always stay out of the right side of the lane.
Always stay out of the center of the lane.
Use the safest part of the lane for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest part of the lane for current conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve inexperienced riders on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: After drinking, what reduces the effects of alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing speeds this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects in your body.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves arms exposed.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Wear sturdy boots or shoes tall enough to cover and support your ankles. Boots should have low heels to avoid catching on foot pegs. Leather gloves or other durable material protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Skip using turn signals when changing lanes.
Look only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect your face in a crash.
Does not protect as well as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also protects from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not apply brakes, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: The center of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place for a motorcycle to ride.
Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
Often has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. Unless the road is wet, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. Still avoid large buildup of oil and grease, often found at intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip of a motorcycle. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?

options.text: More often than the amount time spent looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This helps you see hazards behind you.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do to improve safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights show the road ahead, and their taillights bounce if they hit bumps.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries during a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
